source.value:
First, we find the matrix $\, A-\lambda I \mathbin{:}$
﻿﻿﻿![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14069304/assets/947389b453c22e1b56704ec6a1cdf8e7e529ea9a944c57d3e55a471ab3539569.png)

The characteristic equation is $\det(A-\lambda I) = 0.$ 

Since the determinant of a triangular (or diagonal) matrix is given by the product of the entries on the main diagonal, we obtain the following: 

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-9-\lambda  & 4 & 8 \\ 0 & 9-\lambda  & -7 \\ 0 & 0 & 6-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-9-\lambda )(9-\lambda )(6-\lambda ) & =0 \\ (\lambda +9)(\lambda -9)(\lambda -6) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are $\lambda_1=-9,$ $\lambda_2=9,$ and $\lambda_3=6.$ 

**Note:** The eigenvalues of a triangular (or diagonal) matrix are always the entries on the main diagonal.

First, we find the matrix $\, P-\lambda I \mathbin{:}$
﻿﻿﻿![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14069304/assets/8ee9ef991440e5641d6a458c0384382b54eb3d8504856b942fc33cf24b0b85e9.png)

The characteristic equation is $\det(P-\lambda I) = 0.$ 

Notice that we can expand the $4 \times 4$ determinant across the $1$st column, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(P-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}3-\lambda  & 0 & -8 & -2 \\ 0 & -1-\lambda  & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 4-\lambda  & 0 \\ 0 & 7 & -3 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (3-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}-1-\lambda  & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & 4-\lambda  & 0 \\ 7 & -3 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, expanding the $3 \times 3$ determinant across the $2$nd row, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}(3-\lambda )\cdot (4-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}-1-\lambda  & 5 \\ 7 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (3-\lambda )(4-\lambda )((-1-\lambda )(1-\lambda )-35) & =0 \\ (3-\lambda )(4-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-36) & =0 \\ (\lambda -3)(\lambda -4)(\lambda -6)(\lambda +6) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

So, the eigenvalues of $P$ are $\lambda=3,$ $\lambda=4,$ $\lambda=6,$ and $\lambda=-6$ (all with algebraic multiplicity $1$).

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."
